page: Amazon Web Services c5.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8223CL processor with 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark extended instructions scoring in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also a notable strength, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 3707.05 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 92.77 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core performance, fall into the average range. Additionally, text generation speeds for large language models are weak, with the medium 7B model achieving only 6.95 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5.18xlarge offers high compute density and strong multi-threaded capabilities relative to its memory footprint, making it a viable option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory allocations. The instance is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, multi-threaded batch processing, and CPU-bound scientific modeling. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or real-time LLM text generation due to its 2.0 GB per core memory constraint and weak text generation benchmarks.
